notes: All 289 pieces from the parts list are present as b1..b289, numbered in build order. I checked counts per type and colour against the inventory.
I wrote one joined edge per pair of connected pieces with a representative stack, side-stud or pin join. Ports are mostly null. The edges do not list every individual stud.

The booklet's pictures are small. Where the exact base plate a sub-assembly or tile sits on was unclear, I picked the most plausible neighbouring plate. This affects the placement of the grey tiles and jumpers (b34-b65), the Reichstag towers and ring walls, the Victory Column base, the DB Tower foot, the TV Tower cone and the Brandenburg Gate wings.
The Berlin tile (b30) rests on two 1x4 plates (b28, b29). The three 1x8 and 1x4 front tiles (b27, b31, b32, b33) are attached to the side studs of the 2x6 plates with side studs.
The Victory Column base plate (b148) is attached to the 2x2 tile with top pin (b50) with ports left null. Any pin or stud fit there is a guess.

The Deutsche Bahn tower core is built from stacked modules, each two 1x1 side-stud bricks over two stacked 1x2 plates. The 2x10 plate (b178) is joined to all ten side studs. The two facade strips and the ten curved bricks are joined to that plate, which is a simplification of the pictures.
The inverted 2x2 tile (b158) has only anti-studs in the catalogue, so its joins to the brick and side-stud bricks above it use null ports.

The TV Tower trunk is five white connector tubes joined by four black pins. Half pins sit at the bottom and top. The cone and the Bar 6L at the base, and the sphere bar (b218) into the top pin, are my reading of the pictures.

In the Brandenburg Gate, the 24 tan round plates form 12 stacks of 2: 6 for the left wing and 6 for the right. They are capped by 8 sand green slopes and 2 tiles. The two spindled fences carry 8 round plates and 3 tiles. The quadriga assembly (sand green plate, two clip plates, jumper plate, clip tile) sits on the last two round plates.
